hero.lead: A nation of 38.4 million between the Atlantic and the Atlas, trusted with a $4.5 billion IMF Flexible Credit Line and building one of Africa’s largest clean-energy systems.

capital.heading: Morocco borrows on the strength of its policies. Next, a safe toilet in every home.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 63 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Olive groves and green terraced fields in the foothills of the Atlas, Morocco

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Cedar forest in the Middle Atlas, Morocco

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: A reservoir behind a dam in the Atlas Mountains, Morocco

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: The Noor Ouarzazate concentrated solar power complex in the Moroccan desert

items.name: The enterprises building Perfect Morocco
items.text: The Stewards are verifying the companies and social enterprises already delivering the seven basic living standards in Morocco. Suggest one to include.

coverage.gap_text: Moroccans without a safely managed toilet at home: 92 in every hundred.
